skill.name: cold-email-craft
skill.description: Draft a signal-anchored cold email or a four-touch follow-up sequence with the JMC framework. Use a recent public signal, a specific operational pain, a concise value proposition, and a binary call to action.
skill.summary: Create concise, signal-based cold emails and follow-up sequences with clear validation checks.
skill.author: cmj-hub

content.value_statement: Generic outreach is easy to ignore and difficult to validate. This skill turns a recent public signal into concise, specific outreach with a binary call to action.
actual_capabilities: Collects the recipient, company, public signal, operational pain, value proposition, and sender name.
Drafts a single cold email with a subject, body, quoted signal, and binary call to action.
Builds a four-touch sequence with different angles and touch-specific word limits.
Checks word count, banned phrases, signal fidelity, subject length, and CTA format.
Identifies one weak line and proposes a focused rewrite with a rationale.
limitations: It does not independently verify public signals or LinkedIn information.
It does not send emails, manage contacts, or measure campaign results.
It requires accurate prospect context and a real recent signal.
It does not replace legal, privacy, or deliverability review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Turn a prospect announcement, launch, or hiring signal into a short first-touch email.

use_cases.title: Build Sales Follow-Ups
use_cases.description: Create a four-touch sequence that reframes one operational pain without repeating the same opener.

use_cases.title: Review Outreach Copy
use_cases.description: Check an existing draft against signal, length, language, subject, and binary CTA requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Starter Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one cold email using this context: recipient name, role, company, recent public signal, operational pain, value proposition, and sender name. Keep it under 90 words with a binary CTA.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create a first draft from complete inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Signal Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prospect context. Separate the recent action from demographic details, identify missing inputs, and ask only the questions needed before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Early review: validate inputs before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Four-Touch Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-touch sequence for this signal and pain. Use touch limits of under 90, 70, 70, and 60 words, with a different angle in each follow-up.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: build a complete outreach sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Weakest-Line Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this email against the framework. Identify the single weakest line, explain the issue, and provide one replacement line without rewriting the full email.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform a focused ship-or-cut review.

output_examples.input: A marketing leader recently posted a hiring plan for demand generation. The sender offers faster campaign launch reviews.
output_examples.output:
Subject: Demand generation hiring

Maya,

You mentioned hiring for demand generation this quarter.

That usually adds review work before campaigns can move.

I help teams shorten campaign review cycles without adding process.

Worth comparing notes next week, or not a priority?

Alex

output_examples.input: A sales operations director announced a new regional expansion. The sender helps teams standardize handoffs.
output: Touch 1: You announced the regional expansion. New regions often expose gaps in sales handoffs. Would a short comparison be useful?
Touch 2: Teams entering new regions can lose time when ownership changes between groups. Is that on your planning list?
Touch 3: If handoff consistency is already solved, I will close the loop. Should I step back?

best_practices: Use a recent, public, verifiable action instead of a demographic description.
Use the prospect's language for the operational pain and keep one specific outcome.
Run every draft through the word, banned-phrase, signal, subject, and CTA checks.
anti_patterns: Do not invent a prospect signal, role, company detail, or operational pain.
Do not use generic openers, vague benefits, or non-binary calls to action.
Do not repeat the same pain framing across every sequence touch.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates one signal-anchored cold email or a four-touch follow-up sequence.

faq.question: What information is required?
faq.answer: Provide the recipient, role, company, recent signal, operational pain, value proposition, and sender name.

faq.question: Does it research prospects?
faq.answer: No. It uses public information you provide and asks for missing context.

faq.question: Can it write JSON output?
faq.answer: Yes. It can return subject, preheader, body, touch number, word count, and framework fields when requested.

faq.question: How long are the emails?
faq.answer: The first touch stays under 90 words, with shorter limits for later touches.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing draft?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify and rewrite the single weakest line with a brief rationale.
